newsitem.title: USA: Mass. voters approve most local bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Mass. voters approve most local bond issues.

text.p: Massachusetts voters approved most of the bond initiatives offered by five towns at the November 5 elections, according to local officials.
The following list details the election results.
Shall Athol issue bonds for buying or leasing land for a middle school for Athol-Royalston Regionanal School District that would be exempt?. Losing margin: 2,372 against versus 1,879 in favor.
Shall Athol issue bonds to for refurbishing a high scholl that would be exempt? Losing margin: 2,378 against 1,792 in favor.
Shall Berkley issue bonds to pay for a new school that would be exempt from the proposition 2-1/2? Winning margin: 1,186 in favor versus 1,037 opposed.
Shall Berkley issue bonds for new police and fire department facilities that would be exempt? Winning margin: 1,300 yes versus 923 against.
Shall Easthampton issue bonds to build a new facility for the fire and police department that would be exempt? Winning margin: 4,265 in favor versus 2,885 against.
Shall Millbury issue bonds to pay for building sewage system and appurtenant works in the Oak Pond area tha would be exempt? Winning margin: 2,585 in favor versus 2,521 against.

Shall Millis issue bonds for drawings, bid documents, project representations, construction contracts and furnishings for major renovations to the Millis Middle School/High School Building that would be exempt? Winning margin: 2,469 in favor vesus 1,271 against, 218 ballots left blank.
